rows.description: The person I hurt refuses to speak to me. I feel the weight of it. Wise: apologise clearly without excuses, give space, and accept that repair is her choice and takes time. Harmful: pressing her for forgiveness.

rows.description: My family says "we expected better" and I feel crushed. Wise: hear the honest part, share my plan to repair, and distinguish disappointment in an act from rejection of me. Harmful: swallowing it as proof I am unlovable.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, compassion, forgiveness, pride, shame

rows.description: Any error feels like proof that I am a fraud, so I overwork and avoid risk. Wise: aim for good, learn from the slip, and tell someone about it. Harmful: never trying anything I might fail at.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, compassion, disillusionment, forgiveness, pride

rows.description: My mentor says, "I made worse mistakes at your age, now what will you do?" I feel steadied. Wise: use that grace to act, not to dwell. Harmful: hearing acceptance as permission to be careless.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, disillusionment, forgiveness, pride, shame

rows.description: I refuse to admit I was wrong because it feels like admitting I am nothing. Wise: apologising shows strength; my worth does not depend on being right. Harmful: doubling down and losing trust.

rows.description: After my result a friend simply says "come, let us eat" and does not lecture. I feel held. Wise: let the kindness settle me before I plan the next step. Harmful: pushing him away because I feel undeserving.
